markdown_content: ## Making persistent `figures` *What happened to our line?* You may have noticed we did not create any variables so far, and have only been calling `pyplot` **functions**. This is because `pyplot` uses a concept called a "state machine" to store the chart behind the scenes rather than exposing it to the user. Executing a new code cell clears the state and begins a new plot. *What if we want to access our chart again later?* There is a simple way to get around the default behavior of `pyplot`, which is to explicitly create variables to store the chart. Matplotlib calls the elements of a chart the `Figure` and `Axes`, as illustrated in this diagram: (image credit [ajaytech.co](https://ajaytech.co/matplotlib))
